description.purpose: A table a manifest can name: one store cell as a whole template, so a running colony can be given a place to keep rows by a declaration instead of by a hand-built subtree. The shipped table is a generic four-column one (id, at, text, meta) and it is meant to be REPLACED at instantiation -- the schema is the parameter that makes this template useful twice.
description.use_when: Wherever something a colony produces has to outlive its message. Instantiate it under a name that says what it keeps, hand it a schema in the same declaration, and wire the writer in.
description.not_in_scope: No policy, no schedule, no trim, no constraints. A column is text, int or json; PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE and NOT NULL are a core defer of the cell type, so two identical rows are two rows and dedupe belongs to whoever writes.
description.emits_meaning: ONE answer per inbound message. With a single tool_call: one tool_result turn, hop.operation naming the operation (or the literal 'error' when nothing parsable arrived) plus rows_affected and duration_ms. With two or more: one turn per call in call order, hop.operation 'bundle', hop.bundle_errors counting the failed ones, and the per-operation metadata in the results[] slot. A return edge out of this cell tells the legs of a two-phase exchange apart on hop.operation and on nothing else: hop is REPLACED on every emission, so nothing the caller stamped outbound survives the answer, while context is PERSISTENT and is therefore identical on both legs -- a return edge guarded on context matches the write answer too, re-enters the write branch and loops until the TTL (GH #521).
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns whose text is the JSON args of a store operation -- {operation, table, ...}. An insert carries `row`, a select carries `columns` (there is no projectionless SELECT *).
examples: {"operation": "select", "table": "rows", "columns": ["id", "text"], "limit": 10} -> tool_result whose text is the row array
override_params {"schema": {"headlines": {"id": "text", "title": "text"}}} -> the same template, a different shelf
